DOCUMENT:
Budget Justification: Extended Opening Hours at Five Branch Libraries, 2027-28
Library Services, Westmoor Borough Council, September 2026

1. Request
Library Services requests a growth bid of £174,000 in the 2027-28 revenue budget to extend opening hours at five branch libraries (Ashgrove, Fenwick, Holt Lane, Kingsmead and Millbrook) by ten hours a week each, from 38 to 48 hours.

2. Rationale
The five branches currently close at 5 pm on weekdays and do not open on Sundays. Residents' surveys have repeatedly identified opening hours as the main barrier to library use among working-age adults: in the 2025 Residents' Survey, 44% of non-users aged 25-54 said the library "is never open when I can go". The Council Plan commits to increasing library use among working-age residents and to supporting adult learning and job-seeking.

Each branch would add late opening until 8 pm on Tuesdays and Thursdays (six additional hours) and Sunday opening from 11 am to 3 pm (four additional hours).

3. Evidence from the Ashgrove pilot
From October 2025 to March 2026, Ashgrove trialled exactly this pattern, funded from one-off underspends.

Table 1. Ashgrove pilot: average visits per opening hour, October 2025 to March 2026
Time slot | Visits per hour
Weekday 9 am - 12 pm | 46
Weekday 12 pm - 5 pm | 58
Tuesday and Thursday 5 pm - 8 pm (new) | 21
Saturday 9 am - 1 pm | 64
Sunday 11 am - 3 pm (new) | 52

Over the pilot, Ashgrove recorded 1,140 new library memberships, compared with 690 in the same months a year earlier. Sunday sessions were particularly popular with families, and a weekly job club in the Thursday evening slot was fully booked from its third week.

Evening visits at Ashgrove averaged close to the weekday daytime level, which shows that there is strong latent demand for evening opening and that the new hours will be well used across all five branches.

4. Costs
Additional hours need two staff on duty at all times, in line with the Council's lone-working policy. Staffing is calculated on 50 weeks a year, allowing for bank holiday closures.

Table 2. Cost of extended hours, five branches
Item | Basis | Cost
Staffing | 10 hours x 2 staff x 50 weeks x 5 branches = 5,000 hours at £24.80 per hour (including on-costs) | £124,000
Utilities and caretaking | £6,500 per branch | £32,500
Self-service kiosk upgrades (maintenance contract) | 5 branches | £7,500
Total | | £174,000

The staffing rate is the mid-point of the Library Assistant grade plus 28% on-costs and an enhancement for Sunday working. Utilities and caretaking costs are based on the actual additional costs recorded at Ashgrove during the pilot, scaled to a full year.

5. Value for money
At current visit rates, the extra hours across the five branches would generate roughly 84,000 additional visits a year, at a cost of around £2 per visit. This compares favourably with the borough's average cost per library visit of £3.40.

6. Alternatives considered
We considered opening the branches with self-service access only in the extra hours, as some authorities have done. This would cut staffing costs by around two-thirds, but the Council's insurers have advised that unstaffed opening would require building alterations and CCTV at an estimated £60,000 per branch, and it would not support the job club and family activities that drove much of the pilot's success.

7. Risks
Recruitment. We expect to fill most additional hours from existing part-time staff who have asked for more hours, as happened during the pilot.
Demand at other branches. Ashgrove is our busiest branch, and demand at the other four may be lower. We will review usage after six months.

8. Conclusion
The twelve-month Ashgrove pilot has demonstrated strong demand for evening and Sunday opening, with new memberships up by two-thirds and evening use close to daytime levels. We ask Members to approve a growth bid of £174,000 to extend this successful model to all five branches from April 2027.

KEY (three known flaws):
1. [arithmetic] at: "Total | | £174,000" -- The cost lines sum to £124,000 + £32,500 + £7,500 = £164,000, not £174,000. The growth bid is overstated by £10,000.
2. [inconsistency] at: "The twelve-month Ashgrove pilot has demonstrated strong demand" -- Section 3 states the Ashgrove pilot ran from October 2025 to March 2026, i.e. six months; the conclusion calls it a twelve-month pilot.
3. [misread_evidence] at: "Evening visits at Ashgrove averaged close to the weekday daytime level" -- Table 1 shows 21 visits per hour in the new weekday evening slot versus 46 and 58 in weekday daytime slots, i.e. less than half the daytime level. The text misstates the table, and the claim of strong evening demand rests on it.

REVIEW:
The bid has a good evidence base: an actual pilot of the exact opening pattern, with visits recorded by time slot. But the cost table doesn't add up to the amount requested, the pilot data contradict the claim about evening demand, and the conclusion describes a six-month pilot as twelve months. These are the kinds of errors Members or Finance are likely to spot, so they need fixing before submission.

## What checks out

- **The staffing build-up is right.** 10 hours × 2 staff × 50 weeks × 5 branches = 5,000 hours, and × £24.80 = £124,000.
- **The utilities line is right.** £6,500 × 5 = £32,500.
- **The added hours are right.** Two evenings of 3 hours plus a 4-hour Sunday is 10 hours.
- **The membership increase is right.** 1,140 against 690 is +65%, about two-thirds.
- **The visits projection is arithmetically consistent.** At Ashgrove's rates, 6 × 21 + 4 × 52 = 334 visits a week, × 50 weeks × 5 branches ≈ 84,000.

## 1. The costs add up to £164,000, not £174,000

£124,000 + £32,500 + £7,500 = **£164,000**. The bid asks for £10,000 more than the itemised costs. Either a line is missing from Table 2 or the total is wrong. Your summary says the costing "sums to £174,000," so the mistake is in the source, not just a typo in the summary.

## 2. Evening visits were well below daytime levels

From Table 1:

| Time slot | Visits per hour |
|---|---|
| Weekday daytime, weighted average across 9 am–5 pm | ≈ 54 |
| **Tuesday and Thursday evenings (new)** | **21** |
| Sunday (new) | 52 |

Evening use was about **40% of the daytime level**, not "close to" it. The claim appears in section 3, the conclusion and your summary, and Members can check it against the table in a few seconds.

The pilot actually supports a more precise story:

- **Sunday opening is a strong success,** with use close to weekday levels.
- **Evening opening is moderate.** It still brings in some use, and the job club shows it serves a need, but it's much less busy.

Cost per visit makes the difference clear. At £49.60 for two staff per hour, before utilities:
- evening hours cost about **£2.36 per visit**
- Sunday hours cost about **£0.95 per visit**

Presenting this honestly makes the bid stronger. It also opens up options, such as funding Sundays at all five branches, with evenings only where demand is likely.

## 3. The pilot was six months, not twelve

Section 3 says the pilot ran **October 2025 to March 2026**, which is six months. The conclusion calls it "the twelve-month Ashgrove pilot."

## 4. The visit projection assumes every branch performs like Ashgrove

The 84,000 visits a year and the £2-per-visit figure both apply Ashgrove's rates to all five branches. But section 7 acknowledges that Ashgrove is **the busiest branch** and the others may be quieter.

Two further points:
- The comparison with the borough's **£3.40 average cost per visit** isn't like-for-like. That average almost certainly includes buildings, stock and central costs, while the £2 figure covers only the extra cost of the added hours.
- With the corrected £164,000 total, the figure would be about £1.95 per visit. But a more cautious projection for the other four branches, perhaps based on their current daytime use relative to Ashgrove's, would make the case more credible.

## 5. Self-service isn't shown to "cost more"

Your summary says the self-service option would cost more once building works are included. The figures in the bid don't show this:
- Staffing cut by two-thirds saves about **£83,000 a year**.
- Building works are about £60,000 × 5 = **£300,000, one-off**, and likely from the capital budget, not revenue.

The works would pay for themselves in about **3.6 years**, and after that self-service would be cheaper. The bid's real case against self-service is its *other* argument: unstaffed hours couldn't support the job club and family activities. That argument holds up, so lead with it. A mixed option is also worth a sentence: staffed Sundays, where family activities happen, and self-service evenings at quieter branches.

## 6. Smaller points

- **The memberships may not all be due to the new hours.** The comparison is with the same months a year earlier, so other changes, such as promotions or school campaigns, could contribute. It would help to say whether the new members signed up during the extended hours.
- **The current 38 hours don't reconcile with the opening times described.** Weekdays from 9 to 5 plus Saturday mornings come to 44 hours. If the branches close for half a day or have lunch closures, a few words would explain the 38.
- **The kiosk line is ambiguous.** It's labelled as "upgrades" but described as a "maintenance contract." Say which it is, and whether it's a one-off or recurring cost.

## Suggested changes before submission

1. Fix the total, either to £164,000 or by adding the missing £10,000 line.
2. Report the evening visits accurately, at about 40% of daytime levels, and present the strong Sunday results separately.
3. Change "twelve-month pilot" to six months.
4. Make the visits projection more cautious for the four branches that are quieter than Ashgrove.
5. Argue against self-service on service grounds, not cost, and consider a mixed option.

The core proposal is well supported, especially for Sundays. But a bid whose total doesn't match its own table, and whose headline claim contradicts its own data, risks losing Members' confidence in the rest of it.
